title: Supply Chain and Logistics
description: Supply Chain and Logistics develops the analytical and managerial skills needed to design, operate, and improve supply networks. Students study network design, forecasting, sourcing, inventory, warehousing, transportation, logistics optimization, coordination, global trade, risk, sustainability, and analytics-driven digital operations.

topics.title: Supply Chain Strategy, Flows, and Performance
topics.description: Students begin by understanding supply chains as coordinated flows of materials, information, money, and decisions across firms and facilities.

children.title: Supply chain structure
children.description: The point is to see the supply chain as an end-to-end system rather than a set of isolated functions.

children.title: Suppliers, plants, warehouses, retailers, and customers
Performance metrics
children.description: Students learn the measures used to judge whether a supply chain is working.

children.title: Cost, service, speed, quality, and flexibility
Strategic fit
children.description: This subtopic links supply chain design to product, market, and competitive strategy.

topics.title: Supply Chain Network Design
topics.description: This module covers where facilities should be located, how flows should be assigned, and how network decisions shape cost, service, and resilience.

children.title: Facility location
children.description: Facility decisions shape long-term cost, service, and risk exposure.

children.title: Plants, DCs, Cross-Docks, and Fulfillment Nodes
Network flows
children.description: Students learn how materials move through a network under cost and capacity constraints.

children.title: Design tradeoffs
children.description: Network design balances cost, service, resilience, and flexibility.

topics.title: Demand Planning and Forecasting
topics.description: Students learn how demand signals become forecasts, and how forecast quality affects inventory, capacity, and transportation choices.

children.title: Forecasting fundamentals
children.description: Forecasts convert demand history and market knowledge into planning inputs.

children.title: Forecast accuracy
children.description: Students learn to measure error and diagnose whether a forecast is useful.

children.title: MAD, MAPE, Bias, and Tracking Signals
Planning connection
children.description: Forecasts matter because they drive downstream decisions.

topics.title: Procurement, Sourcing, and Supplier Relationships
topics.description: This topic focuses on how firms select suppliers, structure contracts, manage supplier performance, and protect continuity of supply.

children.title: Sourcing strategy
children.description: Students learn how make/buy and supplier selection choices affect risk and economics.

children.title: Supplier management
children.description: Good sourcing includes ongoing performance and relationship management.

children.title: Quality, delivery, cost, and innovation metrics
Contracts and negotiation
children.description: Contract structure shapes incentives and risk allocation.

topics.title: Inventory Management in Supply Chains
topics.description: Students learn how inventory buffers uncertainty while tying up capital, space, and operating attention.

children.title: Inventory roles
children.description: Inventory supports service but creates cost and complexity.

children.title: Inventory policies
children.description: Students learn practical reorder and replenishment systems.

children.title: Risk pooling and service levels
children.description: This subtopic explains how aggregation and uncertainty affect inventory placement.

children.title: Fill rate and cycle service level

topics.title: Warehousing, Fulfillment, and Distribution
topics.description: This module turns logistics strategy into facility-level decisions about storage, picking, handling, packaging, and order fulfillment.

children.title: Warehouse operations
children.description: Students learn what happens inside logistics facilities.

children.title: Fulfillment models
children.description: Different customer promises require different distribution structures.

children.title: Warehouse technology
children.description: Systems and automation shape speed, accuracy, and scalability.

topics.title: Transportation Management and Freight Systems
topics.description: Students study modes, carriers, routes, rates, and service tradeoffs across domestic and global freight networks.

children.title: Transportation modes
children.description: Students compare modes by cost, speed, reliability, and shipment characteristics.

children.title: Carrier and route decisions
children.description: Transportation management turns network needs into executable moves.

children.title: Freight economics
children.description: Students learn how transportation costs and service levels are built.

topics.title: Logistics Optimization and Operations Research Models
topics.description: This topic develops quantitative tools for routing, facility location, assignment, network flow, and cost-service tradeoffs.

children.title: Facility and allocation models
children.description: Optimization helps choose locations and assign demand objectively.

children.title: Routing models
children.description: Routing tools reduce transportation cost while meeting service constraints.

children.title: Network flow and tradeoffs
children.description: Students learn to formulate flows through supply networks.

topics.title: Supply Chain Coordination and Collaboration
topics.description: Students learn why local decisions can harm system performance and how incentives, information sharing, and contracts improve coordination.

children.title: Coordination problems
children.description: Local optimization can create system-wide inefficiency.

children.title: Information sharing
children.description: Shared data improves planning and reduces uncertainty.

children.title: Incentives and contracts
children.description: Students learn tools that align decisions across firms.

topics.title: Global Supply Chains, Trade, and Compliance
topics.description: This module covers cross-border supply chains, trade rules, customs, geopolitical exposure, and global logistics performance.

children.title: Global network drivers
children.description: Students learn why supply chains cross borders and what that adds.

children.title: Trade compliance
children.description: Cross-border movement requires rules, documents, and classifications.

children.title: Global logistics performance
children.description: Students learn to compare lanes and countries using service and risk data.

topics.title: Supply Chain Risk, Resilience, and Sustainability
topics.description: Students examine disruptions, risk mapping, resilience strategies, sustainability, circularity, and traceability as design requirements.

children.title: Risk mapping
children.description: Students learn to identify disruption exposure before failure occurs.

children.title: Supplier, logistics, demand, and geopolitical risks
Critical nodes and single points of failure
Resilience strategies
children.description: Resilience requires deliberate buffers, options, and response plans.

children.title: Sustainable and circular supply chains
children.description: Students connect supply chain design to environmental and social outcomes.

topics.title: Supply Chain Analytics, Digital Platforms, and Control Towers
topics.description: The course closes with data-driven visibility, ERP/TMS/WMS systems, dashboards, digital twins, and analytics for decision support.

children.title: Data and systems
children.description: Students learn the systems that create visibility across planning and execution.

children.title: ERP, WMS, TMS, and APS Systems
Analytics methods
children.description: Analytics turns operational data into better decisions.

children.title: Control towers and digital operations
children.description: The course ends with modern visibility and decision-support approaches.
